original_question: Let X be a Fano variety. Can one give a purely algebraic proof that if X is K-semistable then its tangent sheaf T_X is semistable with respect to the polarization -K_X, and also a purely algebraic proof that if T_X is polystable then there exists a quasi-etale cover f: Y -> X with Y = product_i X_i and T_Y = f^*(T_X) = direct-sum_i T_{X_i}, where each T_{X_i} is stable with respect to -K_Y?
target_in_paper: Problem 12 in §2 (the positivity-of-the-tangent-bundle discussion inside “K-stability of projective varieties”): the paper asks for a purely algebraic proof that K-semistability forces slope semistability of T_X, together with a purely algebraic quasi-etale product-splitting statement in the polystable tangent-sheaf case. ([themoonlight.io](https://www.themoonlight.io/review/open-problems-in-k-stability-of-fano-varieties))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s intended problem: it has the right topic (positivity/stability of the tangent sheaf of a K-semistable Fano variety), keeps the “purely algebraic proof” emphasis, and includes the quasi-etale splitting phenomenon in the polystable case. ([themoonlight.io](https://www.themoonlight.io/review/open-problems-in-k-stability-of-fano-varieties))
missing_details: The paper is not aiming at an arbitrary Fano variety in the loose sense; to make the question stand-alone, X should be specified in the K-stability setting, i.e. as a normal projective klt Q-Fano variety (or equivalently a Fano variety in the paper’s sense).
The stability notion should be stated as slope semistability/polystability with respect to the anticanonical polarization -K_X.
Because singular Fano varieties are allowed, T_X should be understood as the reflexive tangent sheaf, not just the tangent bundle of a smooth variety.
In the second clause, the hypothesis should explicitly be that T_X is slope polystable with respect to -K_X.
For a finite quasi-etale cover f:Y→X, the pullback should be expressed as the reflexive pullback f^{[*]}T_X (or the canonically identified reflexive pullback), rather than plain f^*T_X.
If Y is written as a product Y ≅ X_1 × ... × X_r, then the tangent decomposition on Y should be written as T_Y ≅ ⊕_i pr_i^*T_{X_i}, not as a direct sum of the bare sheaves T_{X_i}.

The natural stability condition on each factor is factorwise, i.e. stability of T_{X_i} with respect to -K_{X_i} = c_1(X_i), rather than with respect to -K_Y. ([druel.perso.math.cnrs.fr](https://druel.perso.math.cnrs.fr/textes/Stability_QFano.pdf))
It helps to spell out that 'quasi-etale' means finite and etale in codimension one.

The phrase 'purely algebraic proof' should be read as avoiding the analytic Kähler-Einstein/Yau-Tian-Donaldson route that presently yields the corresponding metric statement. ([themoonlight.io](https://www.themoonlight.io/review/open-problems-in-k-stability-of-fano-varieties))
refined_question: Let X be a K-semistable Q-Fano variety (equivalently, a normal projective klt Fano variety). Can one give a purely algebraic proof that the reflexive tangent sheaf T_X is slope semistable with respect to the anticanonical polarization -K_X? More generally, assuming that T_X is slope polystable with respect to -K_X, can one give a purely algebraic proof that there exists a finite quasi-etale cover f:Y→X and a product decomposition Y ≅ X_1 × ... × X_r into Q-Fano varieties such that T_Y ≅ f^{[*]}T_X ≅ ⊕_{i=1}^r pr_i^*T_{X_i}, with each T_{X_i} slope stable with respect to -K_{X_i} (= c_1(X_i))?
justification: This is the nearest official target because the draft matches the paper’s tangent-bundle open problem, not the neighboring hypersurface, moduli, or local-volume problems. The surrounding discussion in §2 frames the question as replacing the analytic Kähler-Einstein/Yau-Tian-Donaldson argument by a purely algebraic one, while the nearby background structure theorem motivating the second half is the quasi-etale product decomposition for Q-Fano Kähler-Einstein varieties with polystable tangent sheaf. The refinements above therefore keep the scope narrow but make the question self-contained by adding the implicit singular/Q-Fano setting, the slope-stability polarization, the reflexive-pullback notation, and the correct product-side tangent decomposition. ([themoonlight.io](https://www.themoonlight.io/review/open-problems-in-k-stability-of-fano-varieties))
